claims.text: Hydrogenation of La(Fe,Si)13 alloys enhances their magnetocaloric properties.
Hydrogenation increases the magnetic entropy change of La(Fe,Si)13.
Hydrogenation tunes the magnetic phase transition of La(Fe,Si)13.
Hydrogen can be introduced interstitially into La(Fe,Si)13 using controlled hydrogen pressures and temperatures.
A hydrogenation range of approximately 300–500 K and 1–10 atm H2 can achieve useful hydrogen uptake without material degradation.
Interstitial hydrogen causes lattice expansion in La(Fe,Si)13.
Hydrogen-induced lattice expansion slightly alters the electronic structure of La(Fe,Si)13.
Hydrogen-induced lattice expansion alters interatomic distances in La(Fe,Si)13.
The lattice expansion modifies magnetic exchange interactions.
Modified magnetic exchange interactions shift the Curie temperature toward a target operating range.
Shifting the Curie temperature toward the operating range enhances the magnetic entropy change during a magnetic-field change.
Hydrogenation reduces thermal hysteresis associated with the first-order magnetic transition.
Reduced thermal hysteresis contributes to an improved magnetocaloric effect.
Near the Curie temperature, hydrogenated La(Fe,Si)13 will have a larger magnetic entropy change than pristine La(Fe,Si)13 under identical measurement conditions.
Near the Curie temperature, hydrogenated La(Fe,Si)13 will have lower thermal hysteresis than pristine La(Fe,Si)13 under identical measurement conditions.
Magnetocaloric enhancement occurs only within an optimal hydrogen-concentration window.
Too little hydrogen may produce no significant change in magnetocaloric behavior.
Excessive hydrogen uptake could cause secondary-phase formation.
Excessive hydrogen uptake could degrade the desired magnetic properties.
